notes_for_editor: Tower height is disputed: Dodds' specification says 40 ft, LighthouseFriends 36 ft, NRHP and MHT 51 ft (used). Fog-signal building date: MHT 1901 (also Dodds), USLHS 1904, Wikipedia 1902. Keeper roster differs between USLHS and Dodds for 1853-55, 1881-90 and 1931-44; Wyville appears in a 1831 letter though USLHS starts him 1834. Dodds is copyrighted and paraphrased; the Calvert Journal and Baltimore Sun items are second-hand via Dodds. The 1928 Bulletin item (rescue on 1 July, assistant keeper's wife and daughter) is dated only by the volume year; the 1933 Bulletin text is two-column OCR, and its storm date (22 Aug) differs from the logbook date Dodds gives (23 Aug). The 1931 Bulletin commendation (Jan 2 1931 issue) is for 30 Nov 1930 by inference from issue date. Dodds' account of the 1933 storm carries a 1997 oral recollection by Horace Groom Jr. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, 1917 Daniels) returned no hits; no further newspaper reading done. Kitchen table made of Cedar Point Lighthouse wood omitted. Esther Metivier's recollection is quoted at LighthouseFriends; paraphrased. Disagreement added in verification: MHT narrative gives eleven lamps/18-inch reflectors and electrification in 1907, against Dodds and LighthouseFriends (thirteen lamps/16-inch; 1928).
